target_customer: AI developers, healthcare and life science companies that need expert-labeled data and model evaluation
problem: Training and evaluating medical AI needs accurate expert annotations, which are slow and expensive to source from a small pool of specialists.
business_model: Data annotation and model evaluation services priced per project, delivered through a gamified expert network

founders.name: Erik Duhaime
education: MIT, PhD research at the Center for Collective Intelligence
founders.background_notes: Source: centaur.ai Series A announcement. The company approach builds on his collective intelligence research.

founders.name: Tom Gellatly
education: University of Michigan, computer science and engineering
previous_startups: Sidecar (first employee, acquired by General Motors in 2016)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Managed mapping and data labeling engineering teams at Cruise.

founders.name: Zach Rausnitz
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Self-taught software engineer.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile labeling app plus a scoring and aggregation system that weights annotators by measured skill; standard engineering with the hard part being the statistical aggregation and expert recruitment.

defensibility.rationale: A network of vetted medical annotators with measured skill scores is slow to rebuild, but labeling services are otherwise easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge in sources seen; the company raised a Series A in 2021 and a Series B in 2024.

market_need_then: Medical AI teams in 2019 were short of accurate expert-labeled images; the company reports a network of medical students and professionals labeling through its DiagnosUs app with prizes.

branding.name_origin: The company site describes the idea that a centaur pairs human judgment with AI computing power; it does not say this is the naming story, so treated as the concept behind the name.
branding.domain_note: Company moved from centaurlabs.com to centaur.ai, redirect confirmed by the server in the announcement URL.

identity.visual_style: Clean professional layout with trust badges such as HIPAA and SOC 2
identity.voice_and_tone: Serious and data focused, with a competitive annotation arena framing

branding.brand_signature: DiagnosUs gamified labeling app with cash prizes and leaderboards

rebrands.why: Not stated; both names appear on current pages and the domain moved to centaur.ai

branding.community_and_virality: Gamified app with prizes and a leaderboard for medical annotators, described by Built In coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: A coherent human plus AI concept and the DiagnosUs app give the brand a clear story, but no evidence of broad awareness beyond B2B and trade press.

outcome_analysis: Centaur grew from a medical image labeling app into a broader data annotation and evaluation company. It raised a 15 million dollar Series A in 2021 led by Matrix and a roughly 16 million dollar Series B in 2024 led by SignalFire, with a team of about 45 and an active status. Its edge appears to be a measured-skill expert network, helped by the surge in demand for expert data for AI, though the sources do not give revenue.
notes: The Series A is stated by the company announcement and several outlets; BioWorld reported 12M dollars, treated as an outlier. The Series B amount is as reported in the press release and Axios headline (16M dollars, CB Insights shows 16.5M). A seed round in 2019 appears in aggregator listings only and is not recorded. Aggregator totals raised range from 16M to 35M dollars and are not used. No competitor with a source dated near the 2019 batch was found; competitor lists seen were from 2024 or later aggregators. No acquisition or layoff news found.
